prompt:
Edit the immediately preceding Warden calling illustration to use LESS DETAIL and MORE LINE ART. Preserve the same adult woman guardian, face identity, full-body three-quarter pose, spear held upright, shield resting beside her, sheathed sword, cloak and tunic, stone boundary gate, faint homestead and vertical 2:3 composition. Simplify the drawing substantially, approximately half the fine texture strokes.
Fine expressive warm brown outlines on nearly white ivory paper. Use clear economical contour lines, a few short directional hatch strokes only in selected shadows beneath chin, inside cloak and under overlapping cloth. Keep most face, cloak, tunic, trousers, shield and boots as clean unshaded paper. Hair described with a few larger wavy locks instead of individual strands. No fabric grain, no pores, no dense crosshatching or blanket brown shading. Cloak folds conveyed by a small number of flowing lines. Shield drawn with outline, simple boss and a few plank seams, no woodgrain. Stones with plain outlines and minimal shadow marks, no mottled texture. Distant cottage and hills barely suggested with a few pale lines. Keep anatomy and expression naturally illustrative, enough selective hatching for depth without turning into a thick cartoon or coloring-book icon. Maintain all elements inside frame with margins. No text, border, watermark, color fills, smooth shading or photographic rendering. Portrait 2:3 for final 1000x1500 WebP.
